title: Vasquez: Trent’s communicantur equals imputantur
source_text: XXXV. Similia quoque habentur apud Gabrielem Vasquez, Tom. 2. in 1. 2. Disp. 222. cap. 1. nam verba ista Concilii Tridentini, Quanquam nemo possit esse justus, nisi cui merita passionis Domini nostri Jesu Christi communicantur, dicit idem omnino significare ac si diceret, nisi cui merita passionis Domini nostri Jesu Christi imputantur. Disputatione vero 203. affirmat recte dici posse merita Christi nobis imputari, quum agitur de causa meritoria justificationis, Quoniam imputari nobis Christi merita idem est quod merita illa nobis applicari, & communicari.
pass_a_gloss: Similar things are also found in Gabriel Vasquez, Tom. 2 on 1a2ae, Disp. 222, ch. 1: for those words of the Council of Trent, Although no one can be just unless the merits of our Lord Jesus Christ’s passion are communicated to him, he says mean altogether the same as if it said, unless the merits of our Lord Jesus Christ’s passion are imputed to him. And in Disputation 203 he affirms that Christ’s merits can rightly be said to be imputed to us when the meritorious cause of justification is in view, because for Christ’s merits to be imputed to us is the same as for those merits to be applied and communicated to us.
pass_b_english: As meritorious cause, imputation = application and communication of Christ’s merits.
